architecture.mechanism: A Crowding Contribution Index (CCI) quantifies the extent to which destination stations drive overcapacity flows on preceding links, computed by integrating Automated Fare Collection (AFC) and GTFS link-network data, revealing that the highest contributions cluster in specific stations.
architecture.intervention: Apply the CCI method to the bus network using farebox/smart-card (AFC) plus GTFS/AVL data to compute stop-level contributions to headway irregularity, identify the specific stops and hours whose boarding/destination flows destabilize spacing, then impose targeted holding and departure-pacing at only those high-contribution stops—no additional buses required.
architecture.expected_effect: Headway irregularity is traced to a small set of measurable contributors, so corrective control applied at those points restores evenly spaced arrivals and eliminates three-bus bunching with the existing fleet.
architecture.falsification_test: Compute CCI values over a representative operating period; if the stops ranked highest by the index do not coincide with the locations where headway variance grows and bunching originates, or if holding at those stops fails to reduce the variance of inter-arrival times, the mechanism is falsified.
